title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Evaluating Responses - Cost
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency is evaluating three quotes for commercial off-the-shelf software. The buyer compares the bottom-line totals of the quotes against each other and against historical pricing paid last year. This technique is formally known as:
questions.explain: Price Analysis is the process of comparing the total bottom-line price of a product or service against market data, historical prices, or competing bids without examining the individual components of the cost.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A procurement officer asks a vendor to submit a detailed breakdown of their direct labor rates, raw material costs, overhead multipliers, and profit margin. The officer is preparing to conduct a:
questions.explain: Cost Analysis is the evaluation of the separate, specific elements that make up a vendor's total price (labor, materials, overhead, profit) to determine if they are fair and reasonable.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Under which sourcing scenario is conducting a detailed Cost Analysis most critical?
options: When procuring standard office supplies via an IFB
When a Sole Source contract is being negotiated, as no market competition exists to validate the final price
When conducting an RFQ for micro-purchases under $1,000
When buying fuel using daily commodity market index pricing
questions.explain: Because sole source procurements lack market competition to naturally drive prices to a fair level, the buyer must rely on Cost Analysis to ensure the vendor isn't taking advantage of the monopoly and inflating profit margins.
